function: Beam training: NN modules at BS and UE learn analog beamformers online from ping-pong pilots, after a non-learned sensing phase, to maximize spectral efficiency (p. 1, 7).
system: Narrowband near-field MIMO: BS and UE with 255-antenna ULAs, hybrid analog-digital with phase shifters, 28 GHz, 100 MHz bandwidth; no RIS (p. 3, 10).
method: Complex fully connected NNs (N x 128 x 64 x output, ReLU, Adam) updated online by gradient ascent on received beam gain; no training set, no offline training (p. 7-8, 11).
data_channel: Custom simulated near-field spherical-wave channel: LoS plus L=3 NLoS paths from random scatterers at 28 GHz; no dataset; 100 Monte Carlo runs (p. 3, 10).
test_conditions: NNs trained online in each simulated channel, no offline training; sweeps over distance, transmit power, number of beams, tolerance threshold (p. 8, 11-13).
baselines: Far-field codebook search FFC [19], fully digital optimum from SVD with perfect CSI, fully digital power method PM [35], and the fully digital variant of STT (p. 11-12).
metrics: Spectral efficiency versus training round, distance, transmit power and number of beams; energy efficiency; beam-focusing gain maps (p. 11-14).
complexity: Training cost O(J Ta (N o1 + |Gk| oL + sum of layer products)) per NN; sensing O(1); weight count formula; no measured runtime (p. 8).
q1_support: p. 3: "The uniform spherical-wave (USW) channel model [11] is adopted to model the near-field MIMO channel". It is a custom simulator (p. 10: "The scatterers are distributed uniformly between the transceivers."); no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data.
q2_support: p. 1: "without relying on predefined codebooks or training datasets". The NNs are trained online in each channel (p. 8: "the NN models are trained incrementally as each new data point arrives"), so the sweeps are separate runs; no model trained in one condition is tested in another.
q3_support: p. 11: "The following four benchmarks are considered in our simulation": FFC [19], FD Opt., FD STT, FD PM [35] (p. 12). FFC and PM are non-learned, but no earlier learned method is compared; FD STT is a variant of the proposed scheme, and the learned active sensing of [6], [21] (p. 2) is not simulated.
q4_support: p. 8: "the total computational complexity to train the NN at the BS can be" expressed as an O(J Ta (...)) formula in the antennas, the truncated subspace size and the layer widths.
q5_support: p. 10: "All the simulation results are obtained after 100 Monte Carlo simulations." The channel is simulated (Table I lists its parameters) and the paper gives no code or data link.
notes: Included in area 3: beam training for hybrid beamforming with NNs updated online; BS and UE have 255 antennas, so the single-antenna check does not apply. The sensing phase (averaging of pilots) is not learned, and the label Pre-training in Fig. 3 (p. 5) denotes that sensing phase. No baseline is an earlier learned method, so q3 is 0. The HITRAN dataset cited on p. 3 only supplies the absorption coefficient of the path loss, not a channel dataset, so q5 is 0. Preprint arXiv 2402.15634v2 of the IEEE TWC paper.
